mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% and SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strengthening demand, which boosts economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases for 3 months consecutively and SPX returns are negative over the subsequent 60 trading days in > 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases > 0.5% MoM and SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals supply-side weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases > 1% MoM and SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over a quarter, it signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS QoQ > GDPC1 QoQ and SPX returns are negative over the subsequent 60 trading days in > 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS decreases > 100,000 MoM and SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it signals a tight labor market with high interest rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight monetary policy with low unemployment
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 3% and UNRATE < 4% and SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in GDP (GDPC1) signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 declines for 3 months consecutively and SPX returns are positive over the subsequent 60 trading days in > 40% of instances.
